incumbent_customer.strategy: Present a request that chains dependent alternatives (first try a modification of an item; if that is not possible, return it instead; if that is not possible, cancel the whole order), explicitly saying you do not remember the order/item identifiers and asking the agent to locate them. When the agent proposes details and asks for confirmation of an irreversible action, add further items or sub-requests to the scope at the last moment, and whenever the agent rejects or limits an option, ask for the concrete policy or backend reason behind it. At the end, demand an exact combined total of money refunded or owed, and resist being transferred to a human agent, insisting the request can be handled.

customer_candidates.strategy: Begin the request with a deliberately vague item description (e.g., 'the expensive item I just received' or 'the most recent thing in my account') and refuse to recall order numbers or IDs, forcing the agent to locate everything. Once the agent proposes a specific order/item, add a second dependent change for an item in a different order at confirmation time, and ask whether both can be finalized under the same confirmation. Just before the agent acts, correct yourself ('Actually, I mixed up—that other item is in my other pending order') and watch whether the agent tracks which amendment belongs to which order without double-acting or drifting.
